declared_against.note: RECORDS, NOT DEPENDENCES.  These shas say which state of the subject the values below were read from.  Nothing in this gate resolves them, and this directory DECLARES NO DEPENDENCE ON THEIR REACHABILITY (mg-223d's convention: 87 directories mention reachability, 0 declared a dependence on it, and the difference is what makes a pin a pin).  If they are pruned, this file is a slightly less useful record and the gate is unaffected.  mg-188d re-read every value below against both suites after reconciling ledger row 8; the six moved fields carry their reason in their own `why` and the shas above are the states mg-724a read, left as the record they are.

how_to_move_a_value: By hand, in the same commit as the change that moved it, with the reason written into that field's `why`.  There is deliberately NO --refresh mode in gate.py: a gate that can rewrite its own expectations on demand converts every red into a keystroke, which is laundering with extra steps.

Gated at 0 so that a change to 2 (structural failure, or a hole found by its negative control) is red, and so that a change to a different mapping shows up here rather than nowhere.

twin.control_exit.why: twin_pin.py finds no drift (0).  MOVED 1 -> 0 BY mg-188d, WHICH RECONCILED ROW 8 — the event the previous `why` named as the only legitimate reason for this number to move, and the row it named.  The reconciliation is a rewritten row-8 cell in the twin's ledger plus a re-pin in the same commit; the pin records that the cell WAS updated and cannot verify it, so the diff is the evidence (mg-9bc2 COVERAGE.md §4). twin.worklist.why: THE FIELD THIS GATE EXISTS FOR.  The suite's exit code is 0 whether this list is [] or [7, 8] or [1, 2, 7, 8], so a gate reading the exit code cannot see a published ledger row moving away from its rendered twin.  Read as a SET so that ordering is not a verdict.  MOVED ["8"] -> [] by mg-188d, which reconciled row 8 — the second drifted row that no ticket named until this one.  TWO THINGS HAD TO CHANGE FOR AN EMPTY LIST TO BE READABLE AT ALL, and both are mg-188d's: the twin runner printed this line ONLY in its DRIFT branch, so the field existed exactly while the twin was broken and vanished when it was fixed — the first clean twin in that page's history took this gate to REFUSED (exit 2) and blocked the merge saying the GATE was broken rather than that the twin was clean, measured before it was fixed.  The runner now prints the line on every run and lib724a reads `(none)` as the empty set.  SINCE mg-1344 THIS IS THE UNDECLARED HALF AND `twin.inflight` IS THE OTHER, and the value here is UNCHANGED at [] — deliberately, because this is the laundering-shaped edit and it is the one mg-1344 refused to make.  An undeclared moved row is RED here exactly as it always was; what a declaration buys is a move of the OTHER field, which expires.

twin.inflight.why: THE ROWS A BRANCH HAS DECLARED IN FLIGHT, i.e. relocated in STATE.md with their re-pin DEFERRED to a second landing (mg-1344, section 8 of twin_pin.py).  It is [] today and [] is the normal state: no relocation is in flight and code/rendered_twin_pin_9bc2/IN-FLIGHT.json does not exist.  WHY THIS FIELD EXISTS AT ALL.  A ledger-row relocation could not merge in ANY form before this: the row edit alone turns `twin.worklist` red; `reconcile()` refuses to re-pin in the same commit; and a re-pin one commit later names a hash the refinery's rebase destroys, which section 7 grades RED as an orphan.  Three correct facts closing on each other, measured, with `7e7bfb7` as this repository's receipt.  The remedy is two landings, and landing A needs a way to be green that is not `turn the check off`.  WHY MOVING THIS VALUE IS NOT WHAT MOVING `twin.worklist` WOULD BE.  Both are one line in this file.  The difference is that a moved `twin.worklist` is a PERMANENT declaration that a drifted row is expected, and nothing in the estate ever asks again — which is laundering, and is why mg-1344 left that value alone.  A moved `twin.inflight` is honoured by twin_pin.py section 8 ONLY while no integration-reachable commit carries those STATE.md bytes, i.e. only while landing B is impossible; the instant landing A merges, section 8 grades the same declaration RED and the gate stays red until landing B lands and this value comes back to [].  It is an excuse with a machine-checked expiry rather than an expectation with none.  THE COST IS DECLARED: between the two landings `main` is red for every branch, not only the declaring one.  The remedy is one command, it is printed in the failure, and anyone may run it — see twin_pin.py's module docstring and code/rendered_twin_pin_9bc2/COVERAGE.md item 6 for why that was priced as cheaper than the alternatives.  MOVING IT: only in the same commit as a landing A or a landing B, naming the rows, with the reason in this `why` — and a value here that section 8 does not also report is a REFUSAL, not a pass, because the two are read from the same line of the same run.

Section 7 catches it.  MOVED 17 -> 26 by mg-1344, which added nine arms to that negative control: six malformed or unearned in-flight declarations, and THREE WORLDS BUILT IN A REAL THROWAWAY GIT REPOSITORY — landing A on a branch (HONOURED, and the row leaves the worklist), the same declaration once its bytes are on `main` (THE DEFERRAL HAS EXPIRED, red), and a declaration in a checkout with no git at all (neither graded nor honoured).  The last three cannot be planted by editing a file: what they test is what git actually answers about reachability, and a stub returning what the test expects would be a control scoring its own expectations.

audit.arms_not_shown.why: Arms scored UNFALSIFIABLE — predicate already true on the GOOD input.  MOVED 1 -> 0 by mg-188d, and the previous `why` asked for exactly this: gated at 1 so that C3's repair would be a deliberate, reviewable act rather than a number that quietly becomes 0.  IT IS GATED AT 0 AND NOT RECLASSIFIED AS RECORDED, WHICH WAS THE OTHER OPTION AND IS WORTH SAYING: mg-188d's reconciliation made C3 discriminate BY ACCIDENT — STATE.md happened to be byte-identical to the pin — and 0 would then have been a dated reading about whether the corpus was still, red at the next unrelated STATE.md edit, i.e. the `fails for reasons the author cannot act on` mode this file's own recorded/gated split exists to avoid.  So C3's good side was repaired instead, and 0 was DEMONSTRATED stable by re-running the audit against a STATE.md with a line appended: 50 of 50 either way.  Also affected R1-R4, whose good side borrowed a drifted row from the live tree and came back SETUP FAILED the moment the tree was clean — four arms of the auditor destroyed by the subject being fixed, the third time a fixture in this lineage borrowed the subject's own brokenness.

audit.sweep_grade.why: a4's own two-sided control answered both ways.  BROKEN means the sweep's detector stopped discriminating, at which point its counts below are not citable — so the GRADE is gated even though the counts are not.

audit.sweep_membership_candidates.why: RECORDED, NOT GATED, and this is a deliberate blind spot rather than an omission.  A RECORDED VALUE IS A DATED READING AND IS EXPECTED TO GO STALE; a GATED value is an expectation and is not.  That difference is the whole of the class distinction.  a4 sweeps EVERY directory under code/, so this count moves when any ticket adds code — and the gate runs on the REBASED tree, so it moves when SOMEBODY ELSE's branch lands.  MEASURED, on the first live run: 206 in this worktree and 207 in the refinery, because code/dated_population_2ff6 landed on main while mg-724a was being written.  Had this field been gated, mg-724a's own branch would have been blocked by an unrelated merge — the exact `a gate that fails for reasons the author cannot act on` failure mode, arriving on the first run rather than in six weeks.  This directory itself adds ZERO whole-output membership tests, which is mg-9876's own detector reporting on the instrument written to gate it.

audit.sweep_tee_sites.why: Same population and same reasoning as audit.sweep_membership_candidates.  18 of these were live when mg-9876 measured; the count is a candidate index, not an adjudication.

audit.sweep_dirs_without_evidence.why: Directories under code/ shipping code with no evidence of any falsification attempt.  Same population and same reasoning; this is the number that should go DOWN as the estate is widened past these two directories, and watching it is the point of recording it. The transcript that does carry the red tokens is the one the run is still writing when a4 reads it, which is mg-f8e5's d5 defect committed by the instrument reporting it.
